Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman with first episode of a constant, 3-day “blinding” headache, worse over right eye, photophobia and visual “shooting lights,” partially helped by ibuprofen. 
- GP suspects migraine; arranged face-to-face neurological exam and fundoscopy, prescribed stronger NSAID plus paracetamol, and provided safety-net advice.

Problem List:

Issue 1: New-onset severe headache – likely migraine
- Sudden onset on waking 3 days ago; constant, 8/10 severity, improves to 5/10 with ibuprofen.
- Location: global but maximal over right eye.
- Associated: photophobia, episodic “shooting lights,” mild nausea; no vomiting, focal neurologic deficits, fever, sinus symptoms, or positional night-time worsening; sleep intact.
- Exacerbated by sudden standing or rapid head movement.
- No previous similar severe headaches; occasional mild 2-day headaches historically.
- FHx: mother has migraines with vomiting.
- Impression: probable migraine versus other secondary headache (red-flag = first severe episode >72 h).

Issue 2: Combined oral contraceptive pill (COCP) and possible migraine with aura
- On COCP (name/dose not documented) for 1 year, no prior side-effects.
- If migraine with aura confirmed, COCP may be contraindicated; plan to review BP and consider alternative contraception.

Issue 3: Analgesia optimisation
- OTC ibuprofen provides incomplete relief.
- GP to prescribe stronger NSAID (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) plus allow concurrent paracetamol, both to be taken with food.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen 400 mg orally PRN (self-medicated; exact dose not stated).
- Planned: stronger NSAID – dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Childhood episodic pain of unknown cause (resolved); no chronic conditions reported.

Social History:
- Lives alone; works from home.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: approximately three drinks once weekly.
- No recreational drug use.
- No recent travel abroad.

Preventative History:
- Vision check “recently,” no change.
- No information on cervical screening, vaccinations, or other routine screening.

Physical Examination:
- Remote consultation; no vitals or physical findings obtained.

Plan:
- Book urgent in-person appointment for full neurologic examination, fundoscopy, and blood pressure check.
- Start prescribed stronger NSAID; may take paracetamol concurrently; advise to take with food.
- Continue current COCP until review; warn that change may be needed if migraine with aura confirmed.
- Red-flag advice: attend Emergency Department if headache becomes unbearable, changes character, or new neurological symptoms develop.
- If headache resolves before appointment, patient to inform clinic and reassess need for face-to-face review.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: vitals, full neurological exam, fundoscopy, medication names/doses, allergy confirmation of non-drug allergens, immunization and screening history.
● Internal conflicts: none noted.
● Transcript quality: Mostly clear; brief inaudible segments but clinical content preserved.
